title: Electrical links had positive activity associations within reversal and non-reversal bouts after cell and contact controls in 40 and five selected worms
abstract: We tested whether electrical links predict shared calcium activity inside movement bouts after each bout mean is removed. We linked identified neurons in 40 Atanas/Kim recordings and eight separate Dag recordings to a fixed Cook worm map. The fixed coverage rule retained all 40 main animals and five separate animals. Per-animal models controlled both cells, chemical wiring, shared chemical input, atlas distance, mirror identity, ganglion and neurite contact. Mean partial correlations in non-reversal and reversal bouts were 0.0681 and 0.0644 in the main sample, and 0.0720 and 0.0686 in the separate sample. All four nominal 98.75% animal-bootstrap intervals had positive lower limits. All fixed checks had positive mean associations. Removing any one neuron class kept both means positive. No shared node-label shuffle within ganglia reached the observed means in 999 draws. The state differences were uncertain. We corrected incomplete and mixed-use ganglion metadata after the first scores and document the full change. This is a small conditional association. Anatomy and activity came from different animals. Both recording samples came from one lab. Five separate animals give weak population inference; their two-sided sign tests have p=0.0625. Calcium kinetics, movement, common input and optical effects can remain. The result does not establish direct electrical causation or equal coupling between states.
